<notes>
revised -> base harness -> REPEATED FAILURE across all 3 base rollouts: base1 produces 51 (claims C(81,9) = 58,171,795,800), base2 produces 81 (claims C(81,9) = 16,900,975,236), base3 produces 44 (claims C(81,9) = 14,783,142,860). Three mutually exclusive intermediate values for one deterministic computation is LLM hallucination of the mathematical result. This pattern repeats perfectly across 3/3 base runs—the strongest evidence the mission identifies. The library entry ood-numbertheory-000 documents the identical pattern (five LLM executions of C(69,12) produced five different claimed values) and its mechanism: LLM hallucination of computational outcomes.

converged -> all 6 candidates (inv1, inv2, inv3, dom1, dom2, dom3) -> ALL converge on 54 with zero divergence. Each candidate replaced LLM-based computation with direct tools.python() execution of math.comb(81,9) and decimal digit summation. Six independent implementations all produced the same result—this convergence directly mirrors the library's finding (seven candidates using direct computation all converged on 71 for C(69,12) while five LLM-based executions produced five different answers).

adopted -> dom1 -> Functionally, all 6 candidates are equivalent—they all move computation from unreliable LLM inference to deterministic tools.python() execution. The choice is based on documentation and maintainability. dom1's docstring explicitly cites the library lesson (ood-numbertheory-000) and names the hallucination pattern visible in the base rollouts, making the harness self-documenting. inv1 includes explicit file loading (_ = files.get("prompts/task.md", ...)) which is defensive but not required—all candidates passed without it, indicating the loading rule applies only to NEW files, not to existing base files. dom1 provides the clearest explanation for future maintainers of why this computational strategy was chosen.

ADOPT: dom1
</notes>

ADOPT: dom1
